reviews.author: Seth S.
reviews.text:
Let me start by saying this is a beautiful place. Nothing can diminish that, except persistent winds, and when the wind dies down in summer plenty of bugs.
I like it in fall, when the colors really come out. Sadly, the campground with the best colors usually closes at the peak of said colors.
My current gripe is more of a system wide complaint - the new system the state parks are using is flawed. We are talking about an electronic (database) system for reservations and registration. The idea is great - reservations up until like 2pm, then FCFS registration afterwards.
The reality sucks. It is NOT functioning right. 3 times in one 5 day trip at 3 different state parks the system failed to work for me.
You are supposed to call and register for your site if you have been unable to make a reservation. What happened to me is that they were unable each time to register me for the open spot of my choosing.
It is ridiculous. Fortunately, at the other 2 state parks, there were staff around to sort things out. Not so at Lake Wenatchee.
Then, their instructions clearly stated NOT to put money in a registratiin envelope, rather to square up at the booth. But the booth is closed for the season. And the ranger I finally discussed this with offered no solution besides call the phone number, which did not solve the problem.
Finally a maintenance worker told me I could put cash in the envelope, so I did.
I really hope they figure this out. At one of the other campgrounds, I got a look at their system in action - they could not put me in my site for another night until refreshing the page multiple times. Could be a very fun camping season at Washington State Parks.
Word of wisdom: bring cash, and you still can put it in an envelope, maybe.

reviews.author: Mark P.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful lakes I’ve ever seen. The trails around the park were clearly marked and very scenic. I would love to spend more time here.

reviews.author: Dyanne G.
reviews.text:
Unfortunately due to some car issues we didn’t get to spend as much time at the lake as we wanted to. But we did make it up in the late afternoon and I could tell instantly that this would be a wonderful area to have a picnic at. We only visited the beach area but there were plenty of picnic benches both on the beach and in the wooded areas. The view across the lake was majestic and the bathroom facilities were clean and stocked.
Bonus points for having a wheelchair mat down to the water making this mobility challenge friendly

reviews.author: Marisa L.
reviews.text: Went camping with my husband and two dogs here for the first time. This is the lake that faced my fears. I finally went out on a kayak with my husband! Best choice ever. We will be back! Great camping for children! This camp will keep your kids busy all day!

reviews.author: Julia P.
reviews.text: Absolutely stunning views! Great place for a stroll outdoors after stopping by Leavenworth. Ample parking space, a boat launch area, warming cabin, campground, playground, and plenty of tables for picnicking.

reviews.author: Lauren M.
reviews.text: First time staying at this beautiful State Park. We have a 28ft camper and tow truck and fit perfectly in site 177. It is pretty private because of the shrubbery and has a direct path to the restrooms. This site has no hookups but there is a dump station with potable water where we filled up and we have solar panels for most of our needs. We also have an EV truck so we just hooked up to it and used it for all of our power needs. To conserve water usage we showered daily in the public showers which were some of the nicest showers in a state park I've ever seen. There was no fee to use them. Site 177 has a nice open view of the sky and gets plenty of sunshine. Some of the other sites are much shadier but with starlink we prefer an open site and temps still dipped into the 30s at night so the warm sun was appreciated during the day. The trail is very easy to access at multiple points and is terrific for families and pets. There is also a playground near the restrooms on the north loop were our site was. Firewood is also available through the ranger station. We had no issues with mosquitos as it was still quite cool and windy. Beware the chipmunks though. They get into everything left out. There are also active bear warnings so no food left outside. We saw plenty of their poop on the trail but never encountered one. Leavenworth is about half an hour away if you want to make a day trip or need supplies.

reviews.author: Justin C.
reviews.text: Quite liked this campground, a few things to note first about the site then the park. Site: 31. Great distance between tent pad and picnic table with a few well placed trees for hammock/ clothing line. Fire ring was great distance from picnic table. Great privacy (granted the people in the site next to us weren't there). Close walk to bathroom/showers & Trash. Short 5 minute walk to the lake. Park: Showers were actually free. Normally it is pretty windy, but there was no wind both days we were present. Mosquitos were worse than usual, but a constant cost of DEET and a anti mosquito candle kept them at bay, still got bit up a bit. There is a pretty legit store with camping stuff, espresso, and ice cream. Playground near beach area. By the beach there was a dude selling kayak/ paddle board rentals, he does not come on especially windy days. Kind Staff, met camp hosts dog. Definitely will come back.

reviews.author: pbumbarg
reviews.text: This view from the park is so beautiful. We stopped to take pictures and walk on the shoreline of Lake Wenatchee. It was a very nice & clean park. At this time, no one was staying there, but lots of people were walking around. We hope to come & stay in the summer.

reviews.author: cdth（Beaverton, Oregon）
reviews.text: The south entrance takes you to a large beach with a swimming area perfect for youngsters. Rentals for SUPs and other water devices are plentiful. A small store is on site providing beverages and sunscreen, and so on. Sun from early in the day until the sun sets, with shade to be found in the trees on the back edge of the beach. Picnic tables and children's play equipment, showers, campsites. This location has it all. Surprisingly few motorboats on this large (but chilly) lake. A beautiful setting with lots to do, and a good place to do next to nothing.

reviews.author: Richard B（Eugene, Oregon）
reviews.text: Great place to spend a weekend or summer vacation. Nice beach at foot of lake with lots of room for camp sites.

reviews.author: Ann L
reviews.text: We were pleasantly surprised by the state park- it was a last minute decisions but well worth the time. The park is very nicely kept and the view was spectacular. Water is a great calling card and was the perfect setting for an afternoon exploration!

reviews.author: 1010thomasr（Austin, Texas）
reviews.text: Had a great time on the North Loop doing some snowshoeing. Weather was perfect and the park was so peaceful. A perfect setting for preparing for Christmas! Thanks for making this available.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor 用户（作者名未公开）
reviews.text: Great campground! Very clean, and family friendly. This park has sooooo many amenities, there is something for everyone! The campground has flushing toilets and hot showers (bring your quarters - $1.25 for 7 minutes), it is set on a hillside, so those with limited mobility may want to try to reserve a spot closer to the restroom if an uphill walk is a challenge, but there is handicapped parking near each of the restrooms too. The lake has a swimming area, with a large pebble beach (bring water shoes), and an ADA ramp to get down to the water. There are rentals for water toys of all sorts, a volley ball net, horseshoes, and if the burn ban is not in effect, tons of grills and even a covered fireplace! The little store at the lake has basics, and there was a shave ice cart there this week! The park also offers horseback trail rides. All this only 30 minutes from Leavenworth. We thought this would be a quiet stop between Mt. Rainier and Lake Chelan, and it ended up being our favorite stop!

reviews.author: TripAdvisor 用户（作者名未公开）
reviews.text: This park is a gem. The lake and surrounding area are beautiful with a sandy beach, roped-off swim area, and lots of room for children to play. On a hot day, this lake is the perfect spot for both adults and children. Other days when the wind picks up in the afternoon lake takes on an ocean persona. Either way, it's nature at its best.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor 用户（作者名未公开）
reviews.text: We've gone to the park in the winter/early spring on 3 separate occasions over the years, since we stay less than 10 minutes away. I absolutely love this park. The view is breathtaking. There are eagles all over Washington but it's still fun to see them, including the two that were in the trees on the right-hand side of this lake. Being there in the winter, they do require some sort of snow permit. We didn't have one but they had free 15 minute parking spots (maybe 4-6) though we were there for about an hour with no issues (and hardly any people). They have groomed trails only for cross-country skiers.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor 用户（作者名未公开）
reviews.text: This is an absolute gem of a park. We had sites right by the lake and while it gets windy the view and setup is unbeatable. Kayaks to rent, horse riding and volleyball make for a fun family camping experience.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor 用户（作者名未公开）
reviews.text: Beautiful area with stunning lake views. Roads are snow packed. Nicely groomed Nordic ski trails. There were a few people snow camping.

reviews.author: TripAdvisor 用户（作者名未公开）
reviews.text: Stayed here in late June, site #133 on the north side. Pros: clean facilities with free showers (several reviews mention having to put quarters in, but that is no longer the case.) Sites are relatively big on the north side; many with a well groomed tent pad. The lake itself is gorgeous with the mountains in the background. The playgrounds on both sides are nice for kids. The general store is convenient and reasonably priced (for a tourist trap.) Cons: Mosquitoes. Those blood-sucking b@*#ards were everywhere. They are resistant to Thermacells, Off! and whatever other bug repellent we tried. Must have killed three dozen of them and four of them were "juicy" with blood like the one in the picture. It's bad; bad enough that the general store sells a "Lake Wenatchee blood donor" sticker that we had to get because it's true. It can get pretty windy on the south end close to the water. And the water is cold. It is snow melt fed, so it shouldn't come as a surprise. Even on a day in the mid 80's, it was tolerable but still pretty chilly. Conclusion: glad we came but don't think we'll be back because of the mosquitoes. If you do come, be prepared with mosquito repellent and even something like hydrocortisone cream to treat bites.
